stem: Potassium iodide, $\text{KI}$, is used as a reagent in both inorganic and organic chemistry.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: $\text{KI}$ forms an ionic lattice that is soluble in water.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Define enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H_{\text{sol}}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{KI}\text{(s)}$ has a high solubility in water although its enthalpy change of solution is endothermic.

Explain how this high solubility is possible.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Table 1.1 gives some data about the halide ions, $\text{Cl}^{-}$, $\text{Br}^{-}$ and $\text{I}^{-}$, and their potassium salts.

Table 1.1

| halide ion | enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | lattice energy of potassium halide, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Cl}^{-}$ | $-364$ | $-701$ |
| $\text{Br}^{-}$ | $-335$ | $-670$ |
| $\text{I}^{-}$ | $-293$ | $-629$ |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain the trend in the enthalpy change of hydration of the halide ions.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The $\Delta H_{\text{sol}}$ values of these potassium halides are almost constant.

Use the $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}$ and $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}$ data in Table 1.1 to suggest why.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The enthalpy change of solution of $\text{KI}\text{(s)}$ is $+21.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Use this information and the data in Table 1.1 to calculate the enthalpy change of hydration of the potassium ion, $\text{K}^{+}\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Solid $\text{PbI}_2$ forms when $\text{KI}\text{(aq)}$ is mixed with $\text{Pb}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ ions.

The solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{PbI}_2$ is $7.1 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mol}^3\text{dm}^{-9}$ at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Calculate the solubility, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{PbI}_2\text{(s)}$.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
The ionic radius of $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ is $0.120\text{ nm}$ compared to $0.133\text{ nm}$ for $\text{K}^{+}$.

Suggest how the $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$ of $\text{PbI}_2\text{(s)}$ differs from $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$ of $\text{KI}\text{(s)}$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
$\text{KI}$ slowly oxidises in air, forming $\text{I}_2$.

reaction 1 $4\text{KI}\text{(s)} + 2\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(s)} + 2\text{I}_2\text{(s)}$ $\Delta H^{\ominus} = -203.4\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Table 1.2 shows some data relevant to this question.

Table 1.2

| substance | standard entropy, $S^{\ominus} / \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ | $213.6$ |
| $\text{I}_2\text{(s)}$ | $116.1$ |
| $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(s)}$ | $155.5$ |
| $\text{KI}\text{(s)}$ | $106.3$ |
| $\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ | $205.2$ |

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the standard entropy change, $\Delta S^{\ominus}$, of reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to (c)(i) to show that reaction 1 is spontaneous at $298\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The Group 1 carbonates are much more thermally stable than the Group 2 carbonates.

State and explain the trend in the thermal stability of the Group 2 carbonates.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
A student electrolyses a solution of $\text{KI}\text{(aq)}$ for 8 minutes using a direct current.

The half-equation for the reaction that occurs at the anode is given.

$$2\text{I}^{-}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{I}_2\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^{-}$$

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Write a half-equation for the reaction that occurs at the cathode.

Include state symbols.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
After the electrolysis, the $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ produced requires $21.35\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\text{(aq)}$ to react completely.

$$\text{I}_2\text{(aq)} + 2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{NaI}\text{(aq)} + \text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6\text{(aq)}$$

Calculate the average current used in 8 minutes during the electrolysis.

parts.label: (e)
(e)(i)
parts.text: Identify the reagents required for steps 1 and 2.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Step 3 occurs in two stages.

stage I $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ undergo an acid-base reaction to produce $\text{HNO}_2$.

stage II $\text{HNO}_2$ reacts with C, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$, to produce D, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}$.

Complete the equations for stage I and for stage II.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text:
The $\text{I}^{-}$ from $\text{KI}$ reacts with D in step 4. The mechanism is shown in Fig. 1.1.

Suggest the name for this mechanism.
